html:
On 3 December 1967 a team led by the surgeon Christiaan Barnard at Groote Schuur Hospital in Cape Town carried out the first transplant of a heart from one human to another.

The patient, Louis Washkansky, was a 53-year-old grocer dying of heart disease. The heart came from Denise Darvall, a young woman killed in a car accident. The operation worked, but Washkansky died of pneumonia 18 days later, because the drugs that stopped his body rejecting the heart also weakened his defences. Barnard's second patient, a month later, lived for a year and a half.

Barnard had trained in the United States, where surgeons such as Norman Shumway had worked out the method on animals. The operation made him world famous and set off a rush of transplants, most of which failed. The field revived in the 1980s with ciclosporin, a drug that controls rejection. The event took place under apartheid; a Black assistant in Barnard's laboratory, Hamilton Naki, was later celebrated for his skill in animal surgery.
sum: On 3 December 1967 a team led by the surgeon Christiaan Barnard at Groote Schuur Hospital in Cape Town carried out the first transplant of a heart from one human to another.
